candidates.review: Failed the brief. Despite "wings folded tight", the wings came out spread and drooped forward in a mantling or landing pose (1.9 units across, wider than the bird is long), each a fan of soft rounded feathers that matches neither a folded nor a usable flight wing. The crest is a tall blunt block with flaps on its sides, not a spiky swept crest; the tail is a straight flat plank held level; the underside is cluttered with shards (15 pieces after welding, 26 boundary and 19 non-manifold edges). Bill short and conical, legs and feet fine. Not adoptable; a build script cannot fold these wings.

candidates.review: The pose is fixed: the wings are folded tight along the back with no spread or drooped feathers, the bill is stout and conical, legs and feet are clean (three toes forward, one back), and the long straight tail is about 42% of the length, close to the brief's 45%. Three faults. (1) The tail is doubled: two full-width plates (each about 0.25 units wide) leave the rump in an X seen side-on, one rising gently to y +0.18, the other drooping to y -0.40; the top view shows one forked tail because the plates overlap. (2) The crest is a tall upright block with a ragged top, leaning slightly forward like a cardinal's, not a pointed crest swept back. (3) The body is pitched up about 35 degrees rather than horizontal, on long legs. Topology: one piece of 20,864 faces plus one stray triangle (2 open edges), 1.9% slivers; 1.9 units bill to tail along +z (bill toward +z), 1.30 units tall, +y up, feet at y -0.65, symmetric about x. A build script would delete the drooping plate below the rump and keep the upper as TAIL, cut the crest block and add three to five thin blades swept back from the crown (HEAD), drop the stray triangle, optionally pitch the body down 15-20 degrees about the hips, scale to 0.31 m and paint the sooty-front, blue-back split from the palette. Much better than the first candidate; the first generated jay with usable wings.

accuracy_notes: Adopted 2026-10-25 from Meshy candidate 2. At 3-10 m reads as a crested, dark-fronted, blue-backed long-tailed jay, clearly not the scrub-jay; at 40 m a dark-and-blue dot with a long tail. Behaviour (client/src/animals.js): the scrub-jay's group state machine anchored on ponderosa and gray pines (veg.nearPlants) in conifer and mixed forest, cap 60; perched birds work up their tree in short hops and the group glides on to the next pine; ground foraging under the tree. Still open: the head is still large and the folded wing barring is not drawn (tail bars only, lod0); perches are placed in the crown envelope, not on modelled branches, so a bird can sit in the needles without a limb under it; crest is fixed half-raised (no alarm raise); no juvenile. A local birder should check the crest and the sooty-front, blue-back split.
